# 183 — the audit stops being blind to a north-star CTA that isn't there, and starts covering pools on purpose

Risk tier: **HIGH** (verifier-assigned independently). Zero product-file diff — but this changes what the
merge gate blocks on, and NORTH_STAR's policy is "when in doubt → HIGH".

## The goal, in one sentence

Make the rendered audit say **why** a pool-detail CTA check failed — and rotate pool-detail coverage on
purpose instead of by luck — so the daily gate stays actionable and finds the next north-star-surface
defect by routine rather than by coincidence.

## The intuition — and the twist that arrived four hours before the build

This item was written against a specific recurring alarm: the audit's one blocking finding, every run,
was `dead-cta: "Start Earning" (.cta-button-protocol) missing or not visible`. Classifying it by hand cost
a live 7,962-protocol fetch and a read of three call sites, only to establish it was the harness's blocked
network, not a broken pool. An alarm that cries wolf daily is one the loop learns to skim.

Then **item 182 shipped this morning** and fixed the underlying product defect: `.cta-button-protocol`
now *always* renders — the real "Start Earning on <project> ↗" CTA when a URL tier resolves, an honest
"View this pool on DefiLlama ↗" fallback when none does. So the alarm stopped ringing (verified: a full
audit on this checkout returns **1 finding, 0 blocking**).

Which sounds like this item was overtaken by events. It wasn't — 182 moved the blindness rather than
removing it. The fallback button carries **the same CSS class**. So the check that used to over-report now
*under*-reports: on a pool where no tier resolves, the page renders a button, the audit sees a button, and
reports clean — while `protocol_link`, **half the north star** (`PoolDetail.js:517`), does not exist on
that page at all.

That is the finding this diff makes visible, and it is a real one today: of 737 snapshot pools, project
**`sdai`** ($55.5M) resolves in no tier — absent from `data/protocol-urls.json` (475 keys) and from the
hand-maintained static `PROTOCOL_URLS` alike.

## What changed, in reading order

### 1. `audit-app.js` — the CTA check reads *shape*, not mere presence

The pool-detail driver now classifies the rendered `.cta-button-protocol` into `missing` | `fallback` |
`protocol`, discriminating the last two by the adjacent `.pool-action-hint--muted` copy in **both**
languages (`pool-detail-ko` is an audited surface, so an EN-only marker would go silently blind on it).
`dead-cta` is kept verbatim for a genuinely absent element; a new **`degraded-cta`** fires when the
fallback rendered instead of the real CTA.

### 2. `audit-app.js` — provenance, from two independent sources

When the CTA is not the real one, the run records **what prod would have** (does
`data/protocol-urls.json` or the static `PROTOCOL_URLS` literal resolve this project?) and **what this run
actually got** (did the page's fetch of `/data/protocol-urls.json` succeed, fail, or never arrive?). Both
disk readers degrade to `null` on any failure and never throw — a broken artifact routes to
`undeterminable`, never to a false `defect`.

### 3. `classifyCtaKind()` — the decision rule, order load-bearing

1. disk-side undeterminable, or the run-side signal indeterminate → **`undeterminable`, P1**
2. no disk-side tier resolves → **`defect`, P1** (the `sdai` case)
3. a tier resolves **and** this run's own fetch failed/never arrived → **`environment`, P2**, with the
   reconciliation stated in `detail` in the wording `reconcilePrescanFindings()` already uses
4. tier resolves, fetch confirmed ok, CTA still not real → **`defect`, P1**

`environment` — the only downgrade — is reachable through exactly one explicit branch. Never a
fallthrough.

### 4. `ctaFindingSeverity()` — severity is shape-first (the verifier's catch)

The first version applied the kind→severity table to *both* shapes. The verifier rejected it, correctly:
after 182 one of the two buttons always renders, so a genuinely **missing** element can only mean a render
crash, a CSS bug, or the block never being invoked — none of which a failed protocol-URL fetch explains.
Downgrading it would hide a real defect behind causally unrelated evidence. Now `missing` returns P1
unconditionally; only `fallback` consults the table. Pulled out as a pure exported function so the
asymmetry is testable — one test holds `kind` at `environment` and varies only the shape, so the two
severities must differ.

### 5. `computeRotation()` + `product-loop-kit/signals/audit-rotation.json` — coverage on purpose

Rotation now prefers pool ids never audited before, from committed state (`{schemaVersion, cycle, seen}`),
wrapping with `cycle++` when the population is exhausted. State lives beside `audit-findings.json`, which
the heartbeat already commits daily, so it costs **zero** extra deploys; it is written only when the bytes
actually change, and only ever by the CLI entry point — a library `runAudit()` call from any test can
never touch it. The CLI now prints `cycle N, seen X/Y candidates, picked [...], wrapped=` so a reader can
tell coverage from luck without reading code.

## What the verifier independently proved (not taken on trust)

- Re-derived the test tallies (39/39 plain lane, 20/20 new file, 14/14 prescan regression), ran the audit
  itself (103s, 1 finding, 0 blocking, 29 surfaces), and reproduced the live `sdai` run.
- Ran its **own** mutation pass on `classifyCtaKind()` — forcing always-`environment` reddened 5 of 16
  tests — rather than accepting the builder's.
- Verified the KO marker against both `translations.js` and `translations.min.js` (the file `home.html`
  actually loads), and that `.pool-action-hint--muted` appears nowhere in `PoolDetail.js` outside
  `renderProtocolCtaBlock()`.
- Grep-verified that exactly two call sites set `persistRotationState: true` — the CLI, and the one test
  that opts in with a temp path.
- **Found the real defect in §4 above** and failed the build for it. Both the builder's tests and the
  operator's diff review had missed it.

## Two things caught before the verifier, worth knowing about

**`ROTATION_SEEN_CAP` was 500 against a ~735-pool population.** `seen` evicts oldest, so `unseen` could
never reach zero: the wrap branch, `cycle` incrementing, and the coverage signal were all dead code in
production — while passing a small-fixture unit test. Now 2000, with the invariant written at the constant
and a test asserting it against the **real** snapshot.

**`'absent'` provenance could have been a measurement artifact.** The network reasoning holds (the fetch
targets the audit's own local server and is never intercepted), but `waitForSelector` can resolve on first
paint, before the mount effect has called `fetch()`. Rather than assert the race away, a 2s settle-wait
now runs before classification, and only when the value is still `'absent'`.

## Deviations, all disclosed

- Leg (a) attaches to a **shape** check rather than to the old presence check — the spec's literal trigger
  no longer fires post-182. Without this, the item ships nothing. (Territory notes T1.)
- The **`environment` branch was not demonstrated on a real rendered page.** It needs the page's fetch to
  fail while the file still exists on disk for the scanner; the audit's server serves that path from the
  same root, so the two can't be decoupled without a test-only route knob this item's scope forbids. The
  **`defect` branch's real instance was shown live.** Fixtures + mutation cover the rest.
- Wrap-around isn't demonstrable on real data in one session (735 candidates, 2 per run) — unit test plus
  the real-snapshot invariant test instead.
- Full browser lane not run (67 files, timeboxed); the plain lane plus the new and prescan files were.

## Measurement

No Mixpanel metric — loop tooling under the 2026-07-23 pre-traffic mandate (the
142/149/154/155/160/171 disclosure pattern). Honest proxies, checkable at the next heartbeat without a
code read: blocking findings reflect only `defect`-classified CTAs, and `surfacesCovered` shows
pool-detail ids that did not appear the run before. Window: next 3 heartbeat ticks. **Revert candidate**
if the classifier ever downgrades a finding that turns out to be real — a gate that hides defects is worse
than a noisy one.

## Quiz (5 questions — answers base64 at the bottom)

1. Item 182 fixed a product defect and, in doing so, silently broke an audit check without changing a
   single line of `audit-app.js`. What exactly did it break, and why did the old check stop catching it?
2. Which single real pool proves the `defect` branch is not vacuous, and what one command demonstrates it?
3. Why would `ROTATION_SEEN_CAP = 500` have quietly destroyed the wrap-around feature while every unit
   test stayed green?
4. A genuinely missing `.cta-button-protocol` and a rendered DefiLlama fallback can produce the same
   `kind`. Why must only one of them be eligible for the `environment` downgrade?
5. Why couldn't the `environment` branch be demonstrated on a real rendered page in this sandbox — and why
   doesn't simply deleting `data/protocol-urls.json` produce it?
